title: CQRV certificate envelope, schema v1.12.0
description: Report §8.4.2, §8.4.4, §9.5.1, §9.5.3; DECISIONS.md 2026-10-24 (Stage 8a, reviewer decision 3). Written by CQRV.Certify.Certificate.toJson. v1.1.0 (DECISIONS.md 2026-10-25, Stage 8b) adds theorem, obligations and the machine fields of reference_configuration; v1.2.0 (Stage 8b review) adds trust_boundary.front_end; v1.3.0 (DECISIONS.md 2026-10-25, Stage 9b decision 1) lets front_end be the exhaustive-validation wording (n ≤ 16) or the Stage 8b wording (n > 16); v1.4.0 (DECISIONS.md 2026-10-26, Stage 11b decision 5) adds the optional object hardware (`cqr certify --profile`): a certificate without it is unchanged and keeps schema_version "1.3.0" (valid under v1.4.0), one with it says "1.4.0" (hardware present iff schema_version is "1.4.0"); v1.5.0 (DECISIONS.md 2026-10-26, Stage 12d decision 5) adds the optional field diffusion_shape (omitted means "tree"): only a certificate of `cqr certify --shape few:log` carries it and says "1.5.0" (diffusion_shape present iff schema_version is "1.5.0"; hardware optional there), so the tree certificates are unchanged; v1.6.0 (DECISIONS.md 2026-10-29, Stage 14a) adds the required object solution_count {value, status}: status "kernel_decided" when Cert.lean proves hM_count (Network.countSat_eq_card and decide +kernel; `cqr certify --count-limit k`, n ≤ k, default 12) and `cert` takes no hypothesis — the status line is then `certified` —, "hypothesis" when `cert` keeps hM_card (status line `certified (conditional on: solution_count = M)`); value = instance.M; every certificate written since Stage 14a says "1.6.0" (hardware and diffusion_shape optional under it; solution_count present iff schema_version is "1.6.0"). v1.7.0 (DECISIONS.md 2026-10-30, Stage 15b; PHASE2_SPEC.md §A.0.1) adds the optional field uncompute ("coherent": every temporary AND is undone by the adjoint of its compute block, no measurement, no classical bit; `cqr certify --uncompute coherent`, certified by grover_certificate_coherent): only such a certificate carries it and says "1.7.0" (uncompute present iff schema_version is "1.7.0"; solution_count required there too; omitted means "mbu"), so every MBU certificate kept "1.6.0" byte for byte. v1.8.0 (Stage 16b, DECISIONS.md 2026-10-31; the retirement of the omission convention decided 2026-10-30, Stage 15b review): uncompute is required in every certificate (the omission convention of 1.7.0 is retired), solution_count stays required, and trust_boundary.front_end is the proved wording (the step typed term → network is the theorem toNetwork_pred of Stage 16a, applied in Cert.lean to the typed-term literal prog: prog_scoped, net_ok, front_end, kernel-checked); the wording is tied to the version (the proved wording only under 1.8.0 and later, the earlier wordings only before it). v1.9.0 (Stage 17b, PHASE2_SPEC.md §A.1; DECISIONS.md 2026-10-31): the required object grade_ext {two_qubit, t_depth, rot, meas, ff} — the second resource record GradeExt of the emitted circuit, measured by the same scheduler as grade and stated in Cert.lean as gradeExt_eq (decide +kernel); present iff schema_version is "1.9.0" (solution_count and uncompute required there too; hardware and diffusion_shape optional). v1.10.0 (Stage 20b3, PHASE2_SPEC.md §A.4 "Amendments before Stage 20b3" (5); DECISIONS.md 2026-11-12): the pattern Count — the counting (amplitude-estimation) certificate written by CQRV.Certify.CountCertificate.toJson (scripts/CertifyTool.lean count-certify; `cqr certify --problem count` in Stage 21). Stage 21a3 (PHASE2_SPEC.md §A.5 amendment (7); DECISIONS.md 2026-11-13): 1.10.0 admits both patterns — every certificate says "1.10.0" and carries grade_kind, "measured" for Grover (no blocks; hardware and diffusion_shape stay optional) and "composed_bound" for Count; Count's solution_count.status is "kernel_decided" (value and instance.M the count) or "not_decided" (both null: n above --count-limit, refinement (5′), spec.epsilon then the maximum over a, π/2^m + π²/4^m); the envelopes of the earlier versions stay valid under their own versions. v1.11.0 (Stage 21a4, PHASE2_SPEC.md §A.6 amendment (8) and refinement (8′); DECISIONS.md 2026-11-14): the object selection — budget {w, d, t, a}, prefer, order (the four letters in key order), the three candidates (shape, uncompute, grade or null, admissible), selected {shape, uncompute} and the name of the theorem `selected` — written only by `cqr certify --budget w,d,t,a --prefer …`, for pattern Grover; present iff the version is 1.11.0, which otherwise requires what 1.10.0 requires for Grover. A certificate written without --budget stays at 1.10.0. The Count branch: instance {n, M, m, kmax} (M the kernel-decided count, kmax null for the exact inverse QFT); spec.epsilon and spec.delta are reals, each {expr, approx} (an expression string and a decimal marked approximate, never a rational: sin²(π y/2^m) is in general irrational), spec.estimate the decoding; grade is the composed bound of Stage 19a over the blocks (grade_kind "composed_bound"; required), grade_ext the composed second record with t_depth a bound (t_depth_kind "bound"); blocks lists every distinct block of the circuit (name, gates, multiplicity, grade, grade_ext, live_end), from which tests/diff/certify_check.py replays the assembled circuit for the hash and recomputes the composed grade; hardware_perturbation carries a note (the QASM / QIR measure all n + m data qubits; countPOVM reads the phase register only). The Grover branch (every other pattern) keeps the shapes below: instance {n, M, r}, epsilon "0", delta a rational, grade measured (grade_kind "measured" under 1.10.0), no blocks. Hardware fitness is not part of status. "not yet audited" (no kernel check): proof, cpu, theorem, kernel_check null, axioms and obligations empty. "certified": kernel check passed and the axiom audit passed (sorry-free, standard axioms or the trust-boundary table), no obligations. "certificate with tracked obligations": kernel check passed, audit failed; obligations names each one. v1.12.0 (revision R5, REVIEW_RESPONSE_1 §4; DECISIONS.md 2026-11-16) adds hashes.library (SHA3-256 of the CQRV sources the certificate was checked against — every .lean file under CQRV/ and Apps/ plus lakefile.lean, lean-toolchain, lake-manifest.json, as `path ‖ 0x00 ‖ hex(SHA3-256(content)) ‖ 0x0A` sorted by path; CQRV.Certify.libraryHash, mirrored by tests/diff/libhash.py; null only in the unaudited sample) and hardware_perturbation.status (the δ_hw ≤ δ + G·p̄ figure is an illustrative estimate, not a theorem); every certificate — the selection one (1.11.0 before) and the counting one included — says "1.12.0"; selection is optional under it. The hardware manifests cite a certificate by the SHA3-256 of its JSON with hashes.library set to null (certificate_json_sha3_mod_library), so that a library change moves only the library fields; since R11 D1.5 (DECISIONS.md 2026-11-17) the object reference_configuration is set to null in that hash as well (key name kept), so that a re-measurement moves no hardware file.

real.description: Stage 20b3: a real number of the specification as an expression string and a decimal approximation (never a rational).

rational.description: An exact non-negative rational as Lean's `toString` of `Rat`: "0", "7", "7/128" (lowest terms, positive denominator > 1).

component.description: Report §3.3.2, Table 3.5: one component of the budget check; budget null = not limiting (not compared, fits true).

status.const: illustrative estimate from the profile, not a theorem; see hw noisecert for the proved conditional bound

grade_ext.description: PHASE2_SPEC.md §A.1 (Stage 17b): the second resource record GradeExt of the emitted circuit, measured by the same decision-4 scheduler as grade and stated in Cert.lean as gradeExt_eq (decide +kernel): two_qubit = cnot / cz / cp gates (also under ifBit), t_depth = layers of the schedule containing a t / tdg or a T-power p, rot = p / cp gates that are neither Clifford nor T-powers (their Clifford+T cost depends on a synthesis precision, PHASE2_SPEC §C, and is not folded into grade.t), meas = measure gates (= mid_circuit_measurements), ff = ifBit gates (= classically_controlled). tests/diff/certify_check.py recomputes two_qubit, meas and ff from the emitted literal and checks t_depth ≤ grade.d, t_depth ≤ grade.t.

hardware_perturbation.description: Report §3.3.3: δ_hw ≤ δ + G·p̄ (conservative: every noisy operation counts); G = unitary + mid_circuit_measurements + classically_controlled + terminal_measurements (alloc/free excluded; the sum is checked by tests/diff/cert_schema.py); p̄ is a parameter of the hardware profile.

status.const: illustrative estimate from the profile, not a theorem; see hw noisecert for the proved conditional bound

front_end.const: DSL typed term → network: proved (toNetwork_pred; kernel-checked net_ok and front_end in Cert.lean); parser, surface checker and the typed-term printer unverified; predicate_hash binds the source

not.const: DSL typed term → network: proved (toNetwork_pred; kernel-checked net_ok and front_end in Cert.lean); parser, surface checker and the typed-term printer unverified; predicate_hash binds the source

uncompute.description: PHASE2_SPEC.md §A.0.1 (Stage 15b): the uncomputation mode of the certified circuit (required in every certificate since 1.8.0, Stage 16b; under 1.7.0 written for coherent certificates only, omitted meaning "mbu"): "coherent" = every temporary AND undone by the adjoint of its compute block (4 more T per AND, no measurement, no classical bit; `cqr certify --uncompute coherent`), certified by grover_certificate_coherent through grover_parametric_lemma_gen and Lemma 6.3.2 in mode coherent. The tool writes only "coherent"; "mbu" is accepted for hand-written envelopes.

solution_count.description: Report §8.2, §5.1.3 (Stage 14a): how the solution count M of the instance was obtained. kernel_decided: Cert.lean proves hM_count : (Finset.univ.filter …).card = M from Network.countSat_eq_card by decide +kernel (the kernel evaluates the network on all 2^n inputs) and theorem cert has no hypothesis; hypothesis: cert takes hM_card as a hypothesis (supplied, never decided; the only form before Stage 14a and the form for n > --count-limit). value equals instance.M (checked by tests/diff/certify_check.py). Stage 21a3 (PHASE2_SPEC.md §A.5 (5′)), pattern Count only: not_decided — n above --count-limit, `cert` only (no hM_count, no cert_count), value and instance.M null.

diffusion_shape.description: Report §8.2, §8.4.1 (Stage 12d): the diffusion of the certified Grover circuit when it is not the V1 balanced tree (omitted means "tree"): "few:log" = the few-ancilla MCZ of Khattar–Gidney 2025 §5.3 with Maslov 2016 relative-phase Toffoli pairs (at most 2 clean ancillae), certified by grover_certificate_few_all (KG Theorem 5.1 for every n, Stage 13a; no per-instance classical check since Stage 13a′; Stage 12d certificates used grover_certificate_few with the classical KG step checked for their n).

hardware.description: Report §3.3.2–3.3.3, §5.3.1, §9.5.3 (Stage 11b): the measured grade against a declared hardware profile (profiles/<name>.json, docs/profile.schema.json) and the exact bound δ_hw = δ + G·p̄ (G = hardware_perturbation.G); vacuous when δ_hw ≥ 1; p_bar, delta_hw and vacuous null when the profile gives no p̄. profile_hash: SHA3-256 of the profile file with LF line endings. A check against declared figures, not a proof about hardware; not part of status. tests/diff/certify_check.py recomputes every field.

note.const: routing, native gates and calibration are outside the trust boundary

instance.description: The instance: {n, M, r} for Grover, {n, M, m, kmax} for Count (the pattern branch below fixes the shape).

spec.description: The specification: {epsilon "0", delta, success_probability} as rationals for Grover; {epsilon {expr, approx}, delta {expr, approx}, estimate} with real ε, δ for Count (the pattern branch below fixes the shape).

grade_ext.description: PHASE2_SPEC.md §A.1 (Stage 17b): the second resource record GradeExt {two_qubit, t_depth, rot, meas, ff}; measured for Grover (stated in Cert.lean as gradeExt_eq, decide +kernel), composed for Count with t_depth a bound (t_depth_kind "bound"; gradeExt_bound in Cert.lean). The pattern branch below fixes the shape.

grade_kind.description: Stage 20b3, Stage 21a3: how grade was obtained — "composed_bound" (the Stage 19a bound init ⊕ Σ 2^j • block_j ⊕ inv over the blocks, grade_le in Cert.lean; required for pattern Count) or "measured" (the scheduler on the whole circuit, grade_eq in Cert.lean; required for every other pattern since Stage 21a3). Required under 1.10.0 and allowed only there.

selection.description: Stage 21a4 (PHASE2_SPEC.md §A.6 amendment (8), refinement (8′)): the certified selection of `cqr certify --budget w,d,t,a --prefer width|depth|t|anc` — the budget (the component-wise order of report §3.1.2), the preference, order (the four letters w d t a in key order, the preferred one first), the three candidates in the order treeMbu (tree, mbu), treeCoherent (tree, coherent), fewLogMbu (few:log, mbu) with their measured grades (null when the builder failed at the instance) and admissibility (grade ≤ budget), the selected candidate (the least key among the admissible ones, ties by list order) and the name of the kernel-checked theorem `selected` of Cert.lean (no admissible candidate has a key strictly below the chosen one; `chosen_fits`: the chosen grade fits the budget). tests/diff/select_check.py checks the rules the schema cannot express (admissible, order, the choice against its own argmin).

blocks.description: Stage 20b3: every distinct block of the counting circuit in program order (h_layer, cg_0 … cg_{m−1}, inverse), each a literal of Cert.lean with its _ok link, grade_eq, gradeExt_eq and liveEnd: name, gates (the literal's length), multiplicity (2^j for the controlled iterate j, 1 otherwise), grade and grade_ext (measured per block), live_end (0: the composed bound's hypothesis). The assembled circuit is the fold of the blocks with their multiplicities and classical-bit shifts; tests/diff/certify_check.py replays it for the circuit hash and recomputes the composed grade.

hardware_perturbation.description: Report §3.3.3: δ_hw ≤ δ + G·p̄; the pattern branch below fixes the shape (Count adds a note).

grade.description: The grade (w, d, t, a) of the emitted circuit (report §3.1.1): measured by the scheduler on the whole circuit (grade_kind "measured", stated in Cert.lean as grade_eq) or, for pattern Count, the Stage 19a composed bound over the blocks (grade_kind "composed_bound", grade_le in Cert.lean; PHASE2_SPEC.md §A.4). grade_kind says which.

hashes.description: SHA3-256, lower-case hex. predicate: DSL source with LF line endings; circuit: compact sorted-key IR JSON; proof: certificate .lean file with the pinned configuration (Stage 8b; null before); library (R5, required under 1.12.0): the CQRV sources the certificate was checked against — the preimage `path ‖ 0x00 ‖ hex(SHA3-256(content)) ‖ 0x0A` over every .lean file under CQRV/ and Apps/ plus lakefile.lean, lean-toolchain and lake-manifest.json, sorted by path (UTF-8 byte order, `/` separators, paths relative to the project root), content as bytes (CQRV.Certify.libraryHash; tests/diff/libhash.py mirrors it and checks the recorded hashes against the tree, blocking with --release); null only in the unaudited sample.

anyOf.const: DSL typed term → network: proved (toNetwork_pred; kernel-checked net_ok and front_end in Cert.lean); parser, surface checker and the typed-term printer unverified; predicate_hash binds the source
DSL → network (toNetwork) unverified; predicate_hash binds the source

anyOf.pattern: ^DSL → network: exhaustively validated \(2\^([0-9]|1[0-6]) inputs\) by the unverified evaluator; not kernel-checked$

kernel_check.description: Report §9.5.1: wall_ms = wall time of `lake env lean Cert.lean` (process start, imports, elaboration, kernel) — or, when statistic names scripts/bench_all.py (R11 D1.5, `cqr certify --kernel-check-from`), the driver's wall of `lean` run directly, 1–2 s less; kernel_ms = `type checking` of the Lean profiler in both; statistic says how runs were aggregated (scripts/bench_kernel.sh: median of 5, first run excluded; the driver: median of 5 after 1 warm-up); commit (optional, R11 D1.5) = the commit the driver measured at. Timing fields: they differ between runs and are outside the hash the hardware files cite.
